name: Soetpatats
summary: Glazed sweet potatoes: thick slices simmered with butter, brown sugar and cinnamon until tender and coated in a sticky caramel syrup.
about: Soetpatats is an old Afrikaans side dish, a favourite of the poet and cook C. Louis Leipoldt. It is made in a heavy pot on the stove or in the oven, and it appears beside Sunday roasts, at Christmas and next to braaied snoek.

ingredients.name: Sweet potatoes
ingredients.note: peeled and cut into 2 cm rounds

steps: Melt the butter in a wide heavy pot over medium heat. Lay the sweet potato rounds in it in one or two layers.
Sprinkle over the brown sugar and salt, tuck in the cinnamon stick and pour the water down the side of the pot.

Bring to a simmer, cover and cook over low heat for 20 minutes, until the slices are almost tender when pierced with a knife. Shake the pot gently now and then rather than stirring, so the slices stay whole.

Take the lid off, add the lemon juice and simmer uncovered for 10 to 15 minutes more, carefully turning the slices once, until the liquid has cooked down to a thick, glossy syrup that coats them. Watch closely at the end so it does not burn.
Remove the cinnamon stick and serve warm, spooning the syrup over the top.
prepNote: Make a day ahead and reheat gently in the pot with a splash of water.
